sentences.text: A major film studio is a production and film distributor that releases a substantial number of films annually and consistently commands a significant share of box office revenue in a given market .	production	filmmaking	film distributor	film distributor	film	film	box office	box office

In the North American , Western , and global markets , the major film studios , often simply known as the majors , are commonly regarded as the six diversified media conglomerates whose various film production and distribution subsidiaries collectively command approximately 80 to 85 percent of U.S. and Canadian box office revenue .	production	filmmaking	film	film	box office	box office	film studios	film studios
The term may also be applied more specifically to the primary motion picture business subsidiary of each respective conglomerate .

The `` Big Six '' majors , whose operations are based in or around the Los Angeles neighborhood of Hollywood , are all centered in film studios active during Hollywood 's Golden Age of the 1930s and 1940s .	Hollywood	Hollywood	film	film	Big Six	#Current	Los Angeles	Los Angeles	film studios	film studios

In three cases -- 20th Century Fox , Warner Bros. , and Paramount -- the studios were one of the `` Big Five '' majors during that era as well .	20th Century Fox	20th Century Fox	Paramount	Paramount Pictures

In two cases -- Columbia and Universal -- the studios were also considered majors , but in the next tier down , part of the `` Little Three '' .	Columbia	Columbia Pictures	Universal	Universal Pictures

In the sixth case , Walt Disney Studios was an independent production company during the Golden Age ; it was an important Hollywood entity , but not a major .	Hollywood	Hollywood	production	filmmaking	Walt Disney Studios	Walt Disney Studios (division)
Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer , United Artists , and RKO were majors .	Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer	Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer	United Artists	United Artists	RKO	RKO

Today , Disney is the only member of the Big Six whose parent entity is still located near Los Angeles -LRB- actually , on Disney 's studio lot and in the same building -RRB- .	Big Six	#Current	Los Angeles	Los Angeles	in the same building	Team Disney
The five others report to conglomerates headquartered in New York City , Philadelphia , and Tokyo .	New York City	New York City	Philadelphia	Philadelphia	Tokyo	Tokyo

Of the Big Six , Paramount is the only one still based in Hollywood , and Paramount and Fox are the only ones still located within the Los Angeles city limits , while Disney and Warner Bros. are located in Burbank , Columbia in Culver City , and Universal in the unincorporated area of Universal City . Most of today 's Big Six control subsidiaries with their own distribution networks that concentrate on arthouse pictures -LRB- e.g. Fox Searchlight Pictures -RRB- or genre films -LRB- e.g. Sony 's Screen Gems -RRB- ; several of these specialty units were shut down or sold off between 2008 and 2010 . The six major studios are contrasted with smaller production and/or distribution companies , which are known as independents or `` indies '' .	production	filmmaking

The leading independent producer/distributors -- Lionsgate Films , The Weinstein Company , and former major studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer -- are sometimes referred to as `` mini-majors '' .	Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer	Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer	Lionsgate Films	Lionsgate Films	The Weinstein Company	The Weinstein Company
From 1998 through 2005 , DreamWorks SKG commanded a large enough market share to arguably qualify it as a seventh major , despite its relatively small output .	DreamWorks SKG	DreamWorks
In 2006 , DreamWorks was acquired by Viacom , Paramount 's corporate parent .	Paramount	Paramount Pictures	Viacom	Viacom

In late 2008 , DreamWorks once again became an independent production company ; its films were distributed by Disney 's Touchstone Pictures until 2016 , at which point distribution switched to Universal .	production	filmmaking	Universal	Universal Pictures	Touchstone Pictures	Touchstone Pictures

The Big Six major studios are today primarily backers and distributors of films whose actual production is largely handled by independent companies -- either long-running entities or ones created for and dedicated to the making of a specific film .	production	filmmaking	film	film	Big Six	#Current
The specialty divisions often simply acquire distribution rights to pictures in which the studio has had no prior involvement .
While the majors still do a modicum of true production , their activities are focused more in the areas of development , financing , marketing , and merchandising .	production	filmmaking

Those business functions are still usually performed in or near Los Angeles , even though the runaway production phenomenon means that most films are now mostly or completely shot on location at places outside Los Angeles .	production	filmmaking	Los Angeles	Los Angeles	runaway production	runaway production	on location	location shooting

Since the dawn of filmmaking , the U.S. major film studios have dominated both American cinema and the global film industry .	film	film	film studios	film studios	the dawn of filmmaking	History of film	American cinema	Cinema of the United States	film industry	film industry

U.S. studios have benefited from a strong first-mover advantage in that they were the first to industrialize filmmaking and master the art of mass-producing and distributing high-quality films with broad cross-cultural appeal .	first-mover advantage	first-mover advantage

Today , the Big Six majors routinely distribute hundreds of films every year into all significant international markets -LRB- that is , where discretionary income is high enough for consumers to afford to watch films -RRB- .	Big Six	#Current	discretionary income	Disposable and discretionary income

It is very rare , if not impossible , for a film to reach a broad international audience on multiple continents and in multiple languages without first being picked up by one of the majors for distribution .	film	film
